definitions.explanation: The act of negating or denying something. In grammar, refers to negative forms of words.
The act of cancelling out or nullifying an effect, action, or statement.

examples.japanese: {打|う}ち{消|け}しの{表現|ひょうげん}を{学|まな}ぶ。
「ない」は{日本語|にほんご}の{打|う}ち{消|け}しの{助動詞|じょどうし}だ。
examples.english: 'Nai' is the Japanese negative auxiliary verb.

examples.japanese: {古典|こてん}{文法|ぶんぽう}では「ず」が{打|う}ち{消|け}しの{助動詞|じょどうし}として{使|つか}われた。
examples.english: In classical grammar, 'zu' was used as the negative auxiliary verb.

examples.japanese: {噂|うわさ}の{打|う}ち{消|け}しに{追|お}われた。
examples.english: I was busy trying to deny the rumors.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{疑惑|ぎわく}の{打|う}ち{消|け}しに{必死|ひっし}だった。
examples.english: He was desperate to deny the suspicions.

examples.japanese: プラスの{効果|こうか}と{打|う}ち{消|け}しの{効果|こうか}が{同時|どうじ}に{起|お}きた。
examples.english: Positive effects and cancelling effects occurred simultaneously.

notes:
Derived from the verb {打|う}ち{消|け}す (to negate, to deny). Very commonly encountered in Japanese grammar studies, where {打|う}ち{消|け}し refers to negative forms and constructions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {打|う}ち{消|け}しの{助動詞|じょどうし}: negative auxiliary verb
- {打|う}ち{消|け}しの{表現|ひょうげん}: negative expression
- {噂|うわさ}の{打|う}ち{消|け}し: denial of rumors

RELATED WORDS:
- {打|う}ち{消|け}す: to negate, deny (verb form)
- {否定|ひてい}: negation, denial (more formal/general)
- {取|と}り{消|け}し: cancellation, retraction (of orders, statements)
